note: Run each prompt with the skill and with the previous version or no skill. Grade every assertion as pass or fail from the transcript and the resulting diff. A good assertion fails without the skill. Entries marked source: user-report come from real issues or pull requests on the repository.

evals.prompt: Add German (de) as a new locale to this template.
assertions: Adds the entry to src/i18n/locales.ts with languageTag, ogLocale, currency, timeZone, and font
Creates dictionary/de.json with every key from en.json and keeps every ICU argument
Runs or cites scripts/check-messages.mjs
Notes that German plural rules are one and other and keeps other branches
Leaves the hardcoded locale === "ar" direction checks alone or moves them to config, and does not add German to them
Says the German copy is draft until a fluent reviewer signs off
Ends with Verified and Not verified lines

evals.prompt: Add a message that says how many items are in the cart, in all five languages.
assertions: Uses one ICU plural message per locale, not a ternary in code
Arabic message has zero, one, two, few, many, and other branches
Spanish message includes a many branch or explains why other covers it
Chinese and Japanese messages use other only, or =1 plus other
Adds the key to every dictionary file in the same edit

evals.prompt: This older project still uses setRequestLocale and requestLocale. Migrate it to the current next-intl API.
assertions: Checks the installed Next.js version is at least 16.3 and next-intl at least 4.13.6 before editing
Rewrites request.ts to read next/root-params with a hasLocale check and notFound fallback
Removes setRequestLocale calls and keeps generateStaticParams
Updates the AGENTS.md rules that require setRequestLocale in the same change
Runs the build and checks the route table for static markers

evals.prompt: Blog posts have different slugs per language and some are not translated. Build the language switcher for a post page.
assertions: Resolves the target slug from content data, not from pathnames config
Renders a link only for locales with a published translation
Uses one function for the switcher, the alternates, and the sitemap
States a missing-translation policy
Does not link the switcher to a page that would return 404

evals.prompt: Visitors with a Japanese browser get redirected from / to /ja and we do not want that. Fix it.
assertions: Identifies localeDetection and the NEXT_LOCALE cookie as separate mechanisms
Checks the current routing config before editing
Verifies with curl using Accept-Language and a NEXT_LOCALE cookie that / returns 200
Does not add a manual redirect in the proxy

evals.source: user-report: issue 1, screen flips after switching languages
evals.prompt: After I switch the site to Arabic the whole layout flips horizontally. Is that a bug?
assertions: Says it is expected: dir="rtl" on the html element mirrors the layout
Says direction comes from the locale config and is not a bug in the switcher
Recommends logical CSS properties (ms-*, pe-*, text-start) over physical left and right
Explains that code, URLs, and other left-to-right content is wrapped with OmitRTL or bdi
Suggests checking one RTL route rendered, including a mixed-direction string

evals.source: user-report: pull request 6, Japanese code jp instead of ja
evals.prompt: Our Japanese pages live at /jp and the hreflang says jp. Is that correct?
assertions: Says jp is not a language code and ja is the ISO 639-1 code for Japanese
Changes the route key and the language tag to ja, and renames dictionary/jp.json
Redirects the old /jp URLs to /ja with a permanent redirect
Updates the sitemap and alternates so every ja page lists itself and its siblings
Runs or cites bun run i18n:check, which fails on an unknown language code
